zh: 每块只有两个字符，块内部不会出现三连；新出现的 AAA 或 BBB 只可能跨越拼接处，所以只需知道已拼好部分的最后一块。
状态取 (AA 剩余, AB 剩余, BB 剩余, 上一块)，最多 11×11×11×4 个；每步尝试接 AA、AB 或 BB，或者就此停止，取能得到的最长后缀，用记忆化搜索。
best(a, b, c, last)：对每种还有剩余的块，检查“上一块+这块”里是否含 AAA 或 BBB，合法就递归 best(用掉一块后的数量, 这块) 并在前面接上这块，保留最长的结果（等长时任取，例如字典序更小者）；输出 best(a, b, c, 空)。
en: Each block has only two characters, so no triple can appear inside a block; a new AAA or BBB can only straddle a joint, so you only need to know the last block of what has been built.

Use the state (AA left, AB left, BB left, previous block), at most 11×11×11×4 states; at each step try appending AA, AB or BB, or stop here, and take the longest suffix obtainable, with memoized search.

best(a, b, c, last): for each block type with copies left, check whether previous block + this block contains AAA or BBB; if not, recurse on best(counts with one used, this block) and prepend this block, keeping the longest result (any one among equal lengths, e.g. the lexicographically smaller); print best(a, b, c, empty).

explanationEn:
## Fixed source and example corrections

The only fixed source is web/content/docs/companies/zalando.mdx in commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc. That snapshot has no separate fastprep or OA LIST original, so the evidence is explicitly marked as MDX, without falsely claiming raw cross-confirmation. The text fully specifies: there are 0..10 blocks of each of the three two-letter types AA, AB and BB; select some whole blocks and concatenate them so that AAA and BBB never appear; find the longest string, and any one of several solutions may be returned; the result is non-empty. Accordingly the site excludes all three counts being zero, puts the three parameters on one line, and outputs the string without quotes. Blocks are not split or flipped, and in particular a BA block must not be invented.

The four original inputs are kept, but the first two original outputs contain identifiable typos. For the first example (5,0,2), the text explicitly lists AA-BB-AA-BB-AA but misspells it as AABBAABBA of length 9; the correct concatenation is AABBAABBAA of length 10. For the second example (1,2,1), the original output BBAABAA has length 7 and cannot be built from whole blocks; the candidates in the explanation also violate the block counts or the whole-block requirement. The site gives AABBABAB = AA-BB-AB-AB, which uses all 4 blocks exactly, and length 8 already reaches the upper bound of the total number of characters. The third example ABAB and the fourth example BB are unchanged. No new operation rule was invented to match the wrong examples. The upstream greedy solutions in three languages may also wrongly use too many blocks of one type; this problem's reference program and checks were written independently, and no upstream code was executed.

## Dynamic programming

The state best(a,b,c,s) records the three remaining counts and the last two characters s of the string built so far (initially empty). Enumerate the next block AA, AB or BB; it must have copies left, and joining s with the block must not create AAA or BBB. Consume that block and recursively obtain the best suffix. Stopping is also allowed. Compare candidate lengths; the reference implementation takes the lexicographically smaller one among equal lengths only to make its output deterministic; neither the statement nor the checker requires this tie rule.

## Proof of correctness

The prefix built so far is valid. A newly added block has only two characters and cannot produce a triple inside itself, so any new violating triple must straddle the joint, and checking the old last two characters plus the new block covers every triple across the joint. The transition therefore enumerates exactly all valid next blocks.

Induct on the number of remaining blocks. With zero blocks the only option is to stop, and the empty suffix is optimal. For any state, every valid continuation either stops or first takes some valid block and then continues with a valid suffix from the resulting state. By the induction hypothesis the recursion returns the longest suffix of that state, so enumerating all first blocks and taking the longest yields the current optimum. Hence the initial state gives the globally longest valid string, and choosing lexicographically among equal lengths does not affect the optimal length.

## Independent length bound and construction

Delete all AB blocks from the final block sequence and look only at AA and BB. They must alternate: after AA there can be neither AB nor AA, so if there is a next one it must be BB; after BB, inserting any number of AB blocks still cannot be followed by BB, because AB-BB contains BBB. So the numbers of AA and BB used differ by at most 1, at most 2*min(AA,BB)+[AA!=BB] such blocks are used, plus at most AB blocks of type AB.

This bound is always reachable. If AA≥BB, build (AB)^AB+(AA-BB)^BB and append one more AA when AA>BB; if AA<BB, build (BB-AA)^AA+BB+(AB)^AB. Checking each joint shows there is no triple and the counts are respected. So the optimal length is exactly 2*(AB+2*min(AA,BB)+[AA!=BB]). The independent oracle uses this counting bound and explicit construction, without calling the reference DP.

## Complexity and full-range verification

Let P=(AA+1)(AB+1)(BB+1) and the total number of blocks K=AA+AB+BB≤30. The suffix is one of four options: empty, AA, AB or BB, so there are at most 4P≤5324 states, each enumerating 3 blocks. This implementation caches strings, and comparing or copying costs at most O(K), so time is O(PK) and space O(PK); the recursion depth is ≤K+1 and the output is at most 60 characters.

For all 1330 valid inputs, the independent counting-and-construction oracle produced a witness, and the reference was run as a subprocess on each one. In addition, for the 164 inputs with at most 8 blocks in total, all block permutations were exhaustively enumerated, checking the whole string and allowing a stop at every prefix, without using DP, suffix states or the length formula, to verify that the enumerated optimum matches the construction. The official data covers the four original inputs, single block types, all boundary combinations, severe imbalance, AB bridging and the full (10,10,10). A dedicated checker verifies whole-block usage, triples and optimal length, accepting every optimal output of equal length; the negative controls respectively split blocks and rearrange characters, and ignore AB blocks, and each counts as killed only if it exits normally.
